@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'EXTRAS-12: ToolMode (open, sandboxed) and the check that refuses open mode in the App Sandbox'
+---
+## What
+EXTRAS-12 (spec: `TestudoApp/features/packages/foundationmodels-extras.md`, decisions D128 (d), D131, D73, D174). This is the root of the mode changes. MT-15 (Multitool), SK-7 (Skills), ACPA-19 (ACPAgent) and APP-19 (TestudoApp) use this type. MacControl and AppleApps use it later.
+
+Add one public mode type and one shared check to the core `FoundationModelsExtras` library target. Do not add a new target or product (D73). The rules work (the hard check, Seatbelt) is not in this task (D174).
+
+Create `Sources/FoundationModelsExtras/Hosting/ToolMode.swift`:
+- [ ] `public enum ToolMode: String, Sendable, Codable, CaseIterable { case open, sandboxed }`. The raw values are `"open"` and `"sandboxed"`. ACPA-19 sends the value in the `_meta` of the ACP `initialize` result, so the JSON form is a plain string.
+- [ ] `public struct SandboxProbe: Sendable` with one value `isSandboxed: @Sendable () -> Bool`. `SandboxProbe.live` reads the `com.apple.security.app-sandbox` entitlement of the current process with `SecTaskCreateFromSelf` and `SecTaskCopyValueForEntitlement` (Security framework). When the entitlement cannot be read, it uses the `APP_SANDBOX_CONTAINER_ID` environment variable. Add `SandboxProbe.fixed(_ value: Bool)` so that a test can fake a sandboxed process.
+- [ ] `public enum ToolModeError: Error, Equatable, Sendable { case openModeInSandbox }` with a clear `LocalizedError` message.
+- [ ] `extension ToolMode { public func validate(probe: SandboxProbe = .live) throws(ToolModeError) }`. It throws `.openModeInSandbox` when the mode is `.open` and `probe.isSandboxed()` is true. It does not throw in the 3 other cases. Each package calls this one function when it composes its tools, before it registers a tool. So the error comes at composition time, not at the first tool call. Doc comments say this.
+
+Docs (Simplified Technical English):
+- [ ] `docs/REFERENCE.md`: add a section "Tool modes: `ToolMode`" next to "## Tool hosting: `ToolContext` and `RunPlane`". Tell the two values, the check, the probe, and the rule that a package does not register a tool that cannot work in the App Sandbox in `sandboxed` mode.
+- [ ] `docs/GUIDE.md`: add a short example that composes tools and calls `try mode.validate()`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `ToolMode.allCases` is `[.open, .sandboxed]`, and the JSON encoding of `.sandboxed` is the string `"sandboxed"`.
+- [ ] `ToolMode.open.validate(probe: .fixed(true))` throws `ToolModeError.openModeInSandbox`.
+- [ ] `ToolMode.open.validate(probe: .fixed(false))`, `ToolMode.sandboxed.validate(probe: .fixed(true))` and `ToolMode.sandboxed.validate(probe: .fixed(false))` do not throw.
+- [ ] `SandboxProbe.live.isSandboxed()` returns `false` in the `swift test` process (which is not sandboxed).
+- [ ] No new target or product in `Package.swift`. The build has no new warnings.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Create `Tests/FoundationModelsExtrasTests/Hosting/ToolModeTests.swift` (Swift Testing): Codable round trip of each case, raw values, decoding of an unknown string fails, the 4 cases of `validate(probe:)`, and `SandboxProbe.live` is `false` in the test process.
+- [ ] Add `ToolMode`, `SandboxProbe` and `ToolModeError` to the public surface check in `Tests/FoundationModelsExtrasTests/Hosting/ToolHostingPublicSurfaceTests.swift`.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter ToolMode` and `swift test --filter ToolHostingPublicSurface`. All tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
+- When the work is pushed, send the commit to the session testudoapp-75. MT-15, SK-7 and ACPA-19 wait on it. #step1
\ No newline at end of file
